title: Structured-output & tool-call attribution — unify metering for embeddings/rerank/non-chat endpoints
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Background: We continue to see discrepancies in usage accounting for non-chat endpoints that produce structured outputs (embeddings + metadata, rerank responses, and function/tool-call outputs). Production incidents and customer reports indicate three common symptoms: (1) token counts in billing telemetry do not match tokens shown in customer dashboards, (2) quota enforcement triggers unexpectedly for customers using rerank/embeddings pipelines that run server-side transforms, and (3) tool-call outputs (structured JSON returned by model) are sometimes double-counted when the platform post-processes and logs the output for observability.

Scope: This ticket covers engineering changes to unify the metering path for embeddings, rerank, and function-call/tool outputs for non-chat endpoints. We will implement deterministic server-side tokenization for accounting, ensure attribution of downstream transforms to the originating request, tighten rate-limit checks to operate on the canonical metering record, and add end-to-end tests and dashboards. This will not include pricing changes or invoice-side reconciliation (accounting team to handle if required).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical metering record produced for every non-chat request (embeddings, rerank, structured outputs) that includes: request_id, model, token_count_input, token_count_output, bytes_output, attribution_tag
Rate limiter uses canonical token_count_total for quota checks and does not rely on client-provided estimates
Tool-call outputs are attributed to the initiating request (no double-counting from post-processing/logging pipelines)
End-to-end synthetic tests that validate token accounting parity between gateway logs, billing sink, and customer-facing dashboard within 0.5% for sampled workloads
Telemetry dashboards (billing-lag, metering-discrepancy, quota-false-positives) added and linked from Console; alerts for >1% daily discrepancy
Migration plan and rollback strategy documented; canary rollout on 10% of traffic followed by 100% if no regressions in 48 hours
tasks: Design canonical metering record schema and wire format (Proto/JSON) — infra
Implement server-side deterministic tokenization module and instrument in request pipeline — runtime
Change rate limiter to consume canonical metering record instead of SDK headers — infra/auth
Modify logging/post-processing to tag logs with originating request_id and avoid re-emitting usage events — observability
Add unit/integration tests for function-call outputs that include nested structured fields
Create canary pipeline and run 48h soak tests against production-like traffic
Update Console docs and billing FAQ to describe attribution behavior for embeddings/rerank/tool-calls
decisions: Do tokenization server-side (on the gateway/runtime) to maintain a single source of truth — avoids SDK drift and inconsistent client implementations
Use request_id-based attribution tags for downstream processors rather than re-computing tokenization after post-processing
Keep current billing unit (tokens) unchanged; only change measurement source to canonical record to avoid customer billing surprises
risks: CPU overhead from deterministic tokenization for high-throughput embeddings pipelines — mitigation: batch tokenization and sampling for low-cost previews

Edge cases with third-party post-processors that read raw model outputs before our logging layer — mitigation: update instrumented agents and provide backward-compatible header for a transition window
Potential race where post-processing produces additional content (e.g., sanitized JSON) — mitigation: attribute any derived content explicitly and document how derived tokens are billed
